scholars: Ibn Kathir says this is a favor Allah did for the Quraysh. He saved them from the people of the elephant who wanted to knock down the Kaaba and wipe out every sign of it.

Ibn Kathir tells the story. Abrahah was a governor of Yemen for the king of Ethiopia. He built a huge church in Sana'a and wanted the Arabs to go there for pilgrimage instead of the Kaaba. The Arabs said no. Then a man from the Quraysh went and made it dirty at night. (Some say young men set it on fire.) So Abrahah promised to destroy the Kaaba stone by stone.

Abrahah marched with a very big army and a giant elephant named Mahmud. People from Yemen and other tribes tried to stop him. He beat them. Near Makkah, his soldiers took 200 camels that belonged to Abdul-Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ.

Abdul-Muttalib went to ask for his camels. Abrahah said: 'I was impressed by you, but now I am not. You ask about camels and do not say anything about the house which I came to destroy?' Abdul-Muttalib said: 'I am the owner of the camels. The House has its own Lord, and He will protect it.' (Told by Ibn Kathir, from Ibn Ishaq.)

Then the people of Makkah went up on the mountains. Abdul-Muttalib held the ring on the Kaaba door and asked Allah for help. In the morning, the elephant sat down and would not go towards Makkah. They hit it, but it would not get up. When they turned it towards Yemen, it ran. Turned to Makkah, it sat down again.
Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was born in the same year, according to the most known opinion.
The book Al-Jalalayn says the church was built in Sana'a and Abrahah wanted to take pilgrims away from Makkah. The elephant's name was Mahmud.
The book Al-Jalalayn says: 'Did He not make their plan go wrong?' means He did, and their plan to destroy the Kaaba ended in failure.
Ibn Kathir says Allah wasted all their work, and they went back with nothing.
Ibn Kathir (telling Ibn Ishaq) says Allah sent birds from the sea, like swallows. The word 'ababil' means birds in groups.
Each bird carried three small stones, about the size of a chickpea or a lentil. One was in each claw and one was in its beak.
Ibn Kathir says anyone hit by a stone was destroyed. Some were destroyed right away, and some fell apart a bit at a time while they ran away.
The book Al-Jalalayn says the stones were of baked clay. Each stone had a soldier's name on it.
Ibn Kathir says Abrahah's body fell apart little by little. They carried him back to Sana'a, and he died there.
The book Al-Jalalayn says the army became like leaves of a crop that animals have eaten and walked on.
Ibn Kathir says later the Prophet ﷺ reminded the Quraysh about this as a favor from Allah. Because of it, they could stay safely in their city. Surah Quraysh comes next to remind them.
